items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: And that's where I met this guy, Marnie Jones.

ctx.x: That you would remember such as Joe Oliver.

Yeah, I was in Chicago when Joe Oliver was in Chicago playing at the Dreamland Cabaret on the Dreamland Cabaret on the Dreamland Cabaret on the Dreamland Cabaret on the Dreamland Cabaret. And that's where I met this guy, Marnie Jones. That's where I met them in 22. Now that's a good little bit. That's a good bit. When I was up there, just like on vacation, you know what I mean?
You remember very well, remember all of these people.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Marnie Jones, you know him? ... [INTERVIEWEE] I know who you're talking about. That's John L's cousin.

ctx.x: Did you play there up in Chicago or else? Yeah, well, I was living there at the piano.
Marnie Jones, you know him? Marnie Jones? You know him? Piano player? I know who you're talking about. That's John L's cousin. Well, I was playing the piano. He said, how are you going to be here?

I said, well, I don't know. He said, well, he was staying. Sell them blues. I said, well, I ain't staying here, pal. I'm going back home and writing my lottery. I was making nice money, you know what I mean? My mother was living. That was my father. His dad. My brother was living. My brother. My brother used to work for A.J. Formback. He was the head man. The head man for the game, you know? He had a lot of money. Take out the money. We had them big tables, you know? He didn't know the big dice tables, you know?…
